action: Update PHP to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 and check for the non-default configurations the advisories describe.
exec: PHP runs much of the web; the critical flaws need unusual setups, but patching is advised. No exploitation reported.
plain: PHP released updates fixing 17 security flaws, several rated critical. Server owners should update.

key_findings: A critical PHP security release is planned for Thursday 14:00-14:30 UTC; the highest-severity bugs are rated critical.
The Register says CVE-2026-115560 is an RCE bug needing a non-default or uncommon setup, with a configuration setting that mitigates it.
heise reports all supported PHP versions are affected and that some issues are critical only in unusual setups.
recommendations: Prepare to patch on release day.

summary: PHP shipped security releases 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13, fixing 17 vulnerabilities, according to heise. heise reports seven rated critical (CVSS 9.2) and says some allow code execution, but only under preconditions and not on default installations. heise reports no exploitation in the wild.
title: PHP releases 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13 fixing 17 vulnerabilities, several rated critical

validation.note: The Register and heise reported the planned release; heise reports the released versions and fixes. php.net notice not opened.
